regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

From 2026-10-11 both channels require at least 18 genuinely distinct relevant motifs in every new 35-45-second Short. Show different subjects, actions, useful details or genuine source-backed tool examples that match the spoken words. Repeated offices or presenter poses, zooms, crops and changed labels do not count as new motifs. This is now a production requirement, replacing earlier planning targets for 82-90-second pilots. Preserve the original recurring presenter and painted-world style.

Ensure visual motifs strictly match every specific element mentioned in narration, directly illustrating underlying concepts and specific claims rather than showing mismatched settings.
Start with a clear, task-oriented hook in the first three seconds that promises a specific benefit and avoids vague introductions.
Include at least 18 genuinely distinct, relevant motifs in every 35-45 second Short; count only unique subjects or actions, not zooms, crops, or label changes.
Show real tool interfaces, screenshots or screen-recordings that directly illustrate the spoken step; never substitute symbolic icons, stock images, or unrelated visuals.
Maintain the channel's painted open-world-game aesthetic for fictional scenes while keeping the presenter (black-haired, leather jacket, cyan glasses) secondary to the tool's branding.
Scale pacing to format: use rapid motif changes for Shorts and allow longer, purposeful demonstrations for long-form videos, without imposing one pacing style on the other.
Place mandatory spoken like, share, save calls-to-action at the format-specific positions; do not replace them with alternative CTAs.
Integrate the presenter consistently throughout the video in useful actions rather than limiting them to the opening or closing.
Prioritize dynamic screen recordings or genuine interface demos over static diagrams; the visual must be the actual tool output, not a placeholder.
Verify all script claims against primary documentation and keep technical jargon out of the user-task narrative.
Ensure thumbnails and hero shots prominently display the tool's logo and name, with the presenter remaining secondary to the branding.
Design explicit, seamless visual bridges between sequential script steps so viewers instantly grasp how setup actions lead directly into core functional mechanisms.

## About

**Fincept Terminal** is a native C++20 desktop terminal for financial research — Qt6 UI, embedded Python 3.11 analytics, one binary, no Electron.

Two editions run on one data core. **[Enterprise](https://fincept.in/enterprise)** is the private, closed-source build the team develops daily, for funds, family offices and research desks. **This repo** is the free AGPL-3.0 edition — learning, personal use, academic research — shipping one release a month.

Use the open build if you're a student, hobbyist or academic. Use Enterprise if you're a firm, or if the terminal is how you earn: AGPL copyleft won't apply, and the open build's real cost is your own data and LLM bills, charged per token with no ceiling.

Fincept account (this terminal): Free, or Pro at $10/month for monthly cloud credits, higher API limits and priority support.

[**See Enterprise →**](https://fincept.in/enterprise) · [Full comparison](https://fincept.in/comparison) · [Pricing](https://fincept.in/pricing) · [FAQ](https://fincept.in/faq)

---

## Enterprise

41 modules across six desks — agentic research, quant lab and backtesting, deep fundamental research, markets and execution, macro and global intelligence, and your own workspace. All of it in a [700-page manual](https://fincept.in/manual).

Monthly billing, no annual lock-in, no seat minimum — **$180–$540 per user per year**, against roughly $27,000 for a Bloomberg seat. Quarterly and university terms are on the [pricing page](https://fincept.in/pricing). There is no negotiated pricing and no separate commercial licence.

Enterprise needs its own account — free Fincept logins don't sign in to it.

[**Create account**](https://fincept.in/enterprise/signup) · [**Book a walkthrough**](https://calendly.com/nikultilak/fincept-terminal-demo)

---

## Install

 
Latest release: **v4.5.1** — [View all releases](https://github.com/Fincept-Corporation/FinceptTerminal/releases/tag/v4.5.1)

 

**Build from source** — Linux/macOS: `git clone … && ./setup.sh`. Windows and manual builds, the pinned toolchain (**CMake 3.27.7 · Ninja 1.11.1 · Qt 6.8.3 · Python 3.11.9**) and troubleshooting live in **[docs/GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md)**. Versions are pinned — newer or older ones are unsupported.

> Looking for the Enterprise build? It has its own signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux, behind an Enterprise login — [get them here](https://fincept.in/enterprise).

---
